mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through lower cost of capital for corporate valuation.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and reduces risk appetite, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises above 4.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) indicates labor market tightness that drives wage growth and corporate profit margins, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, rising real GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signal robust consumer demand that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of late-cycle expansion periods when GDPC1 and HOUST both rise, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong manufacturing activity that supports corporate revenue growth, generating positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns through supply chain stability.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO rises, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A core CPI acceleration (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) signals persistent inflation that triggers Fed rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns through immediate risk-off sentiment.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises above 3.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL indicate an inflation-fighting monetary policy that raises equity discount rates and reduces profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During labor market recovery regimes, sustained employment growth (PAYEMS) signals improving consumer spending power that boosts corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of labor market recovery periods when PAYEMS rises, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
